ai.description: This skink reaches 40–50 mm SVL. It is bronze-brown above with a dark lateral stripe and pale dorsolateral lines. Distinctive features include fused eyelids and a lack of visible external ear openings.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of a transparent, immovable lower eyelid fused into a spectacle, which distinguishes *Ablepharus* from other Indian skinks with mobile lids.
ai.habitat: *Ablepharus himalayanus* inhabits high-altitude temperate forests and alpine meadows in the Himalayas, typically found under rocks or leaf litter at elevations of 1,500–3,500m.
ai.behavior: The Himalaya Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky terrain during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ablepharus himalayanus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ablepharus himalayanus* inhabits the Western and Central Himalayas across Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Sikkim, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
